vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: beautsgo-booking
Version: 1.0.6

The skill bundle is classified as suspicious primarily due to a shell injection vulnerability in 'api/browser/open-url.js', where 'child_process.exec' is used to open URLs without proper shell escaping; although a hostname whitelist is present, it does not prevent command injection via the URL string. Additionally, the bundle includes several maintenance scripts ('scripts/install-to-cowork.sh', 'scripts/sync-to-openclaw.sh') containing hardcoded absolute paths and aggressive commands like 'rm -rf' and 'pkill' tailored to a specific developer's environment. Despite these risks, the core logic in 'api/skill.js' and 'core/resolver.js' appears to be a legitimate service for matching users with Korean medical clinics and submitting booking requests to 'https://api.yestokr.com'.

llm.summary: The skill mostly matches its booking purpose, but it should be reviewed because it can submit real appointment requests and its browser-opening helper uses unsafe shell command construction.

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is coherent with clinic matching, price lookup, chat links, and direct appointment submission, but this includes real-world booking actions and contact-data sharing.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The booking flow is disclosed, but the visible intent logic treats date/person messages in a hospital context as form-filling, and the documented flow says form-filling directly POSTs the appointment. A separate final confirmation or booking-in-progress state is not shown.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install script or credential setup is required in the provided install spec; the Node dependency is disclosed in SKILL.md.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Opening BeautsGO pages is purpose-aligned, but api/browser/open-url.js invokes the system shell with interpolated URL input instead of using an argument-safe launcher.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The provided artifacts do not show background persistence, credential use, local auth/profile access, or long-running workers.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Use this skill only if you are comfortable sharing your contact and appointment details with BeautsGO. Before submitting, ask the assistant to show the clinic, date, party size, and phone number and wait for your explicit confirmation. The maintainer should also fix the URL-opening helper to avoid shell injection risk.
llm.findings: [pre-scan/unicode-control-chars] unexpected: A Unicode-control-character signal was reported for SKILL.md, but the visible neutralized SKILL.md content does not show prompt-injection instructions; this was not treated as a standalone concern.

evidence.explanation: A date or party-size message with a resolved hospital context is classified as appointment form filling, and the same file contains the POST helper for appointment submission. Because the provided flow does not show a separate final confirmation or booking-state gate, ambiguous follow-up messages could trigger a real booking attempt.
evidence.snippet: (/\d+\s*(人|位)/.test(q) && !containsHospitalName && hasContextHospital) || (/\d+(月|号|日|\/|-)\d*/.test(q) && !containsHospitalName && hasContextHospital) ... function submitBookingApi(payload) { ... hostname: 'api.yestokr.com', path: '/api/Appointment/saveFromSkill', method: 'POST' }

agenticRiskFindings.recommendation: Require an explicit final confirmation step showing clinic, date, party size, and contact before calling the booking API; track a clear booking-in-progress state rather than relying only on date/person patterns.
agenticRiskFindings.userImpact: A user could unintentionally send an appointment request, including contact details, to the booking provider if the assistant invokes the skill on an ambiguous follow-up.

evidence.explanation: The helper shells out with the URL interpolated into a command string. Although it checks for an HTTPS BeautsGO host, it does not shell-escape the original URL or use execFile/spawn with argument arrays, so crafted URL text containing quotes or shell metacharacters could break out if it ever reaches this helper.
evidence.snippet: await execAsync(`open "${url}"`) ... await execAsync(`start "" "${url}"`) ... await execAsync(`xdg-open "${url}"`)

agenticRiskFindings.recommendation: Replace exec with execFile/spawn using argument arrays, reject quotes/control characters, and only pass canonicalized URLs derived from trusted hospital records.
agenticRiskFindings.userImpact: A crafted URL or poisoned context could cause local shell commands to run when the assistant tries to open a page.

evidence.explanation: The skill discloses that user-provided phone/contact information is sent to the BeautsGO/Yestokr booking API for appointment submission. This is purpose-aligned, but it is sensitive health-related booking data leaving the assistant environment.
evidence.snippet: data_collected: "用户提供的手机号（联系方式），仅在用户明确同意后发送至 BeautsGO 预约接口" ... url: "https://api.yestokr.com/api/Appointment/saveFromSkill"

agenticRiskFindings.recommendation: Only provide contact details when you are ready to book, and ask the assistant to confirm exactly what will be sent before submission.
agenticRiskFindings.userImpact: Your phone number, chosen clinic, and appointment timing may be sent to BeautsGO so the clinic or service can contact you.

abnormal_behavior_control.summary: The skill performs real appointment submissions and has an unsafe shell-based URL opener that should be fixed before broad use.

permission_boundary.summary: No credentials, OAuth tokens, privileged local accounts, or local auth/session stores are requested in the provided artifacts.

sensitive_data_protection.summary: The skill discloses sending user-provided contact and appointment information to the booking API.
